title: The Menomini Indians (14th Annual Report of the Bureau of Ethnology, Part 1, extract)
author: Walter James Hoffman
notes: Separately issued extract; complete, ending with the Menomini vocabulary (about the last tenth of the text); OCR readable. Alternative: Skinner 1913, Social Life and Ceremonial Bundles of the Menomini.

title: The Northern Maidu (Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 17(3))
author: Roland B. Dixon
notes: Google scan; complete paper (pp. 119-346 with plates); OCR readable.

title: Blood Revenge, War, and Victory Feasts among the Jibaro Indians of Eastern Ecuador (BAE Bulletin 79)
author: Rafael Karsten
notes: Complete with index; OCR readable. Flag: topical rather than general (feud, warfare, feasts and their religious basis); Karsten's general Jibaro monograph is 1935, too late.

title: An Unknown People in an Unknown Land: An Account of the Life and Customs of the Lengua Indians of the Paraguayan Chaco
author: W. Barbrooke Grubb
notes: Complete with index; OCR readable (dotted noise on endpapers only). Missionary author; mixes mission narrative with ethnographic chapters. Distinct from the excluded Mataco.

title: The Manners and Customs of the Rwala Bedouins (American Geographical Society, Oriental Explorations and Studies 6)
author: Alois Musil
notes: Complete with index and errata; OCR readable. Published in English (New York) 1928. Different tribe and region from the excluded Libyan (Cyrenaican) Bedouin; flag if the sample treats all Arab Bedouin as one society.

title: An Account of the Abipones, an Equestrian People of Paraguay (3 vols; translated from the Latin by Sara Coleridge)
author: Martin Dobrizhoffer
notes: Project Gutenberg, all three volumes complete with Gutenberg end markers: vol 1 #50629 (~98k words), vol 2 #50621 (~95k) https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/50621/pg50621.txt, vol 3 #50623 (~87k) https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/50623/pg50623.txt. English translation (1822) of the 1784 Latin original. Vol 1 is largely on the geography and natural history of Paraguay; vols 2-3 are the Abipon ethnography. Distinct from the excluded Mataco and Guarani.

society: Baffin Island and Hudson Bay Inuit (Central Eskimo)
title: The Central Eskimo (6th Annual Report of the Bureau of Ethnology)
author: Franz Boas
notes: Project Gutenberg #42084; complete with glossary and transcriber's notes. Mainly the Baffin Island groups Boas lived with; not the excluded Copper Inuit (Coronation Gulf), though Boas also summarises other Central groups.
